parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by ‘kleptomania’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Outline two of the components that Griffiths (2005) used to define addiction.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain one strength and one weakness of the definition of addiction proposed by Griffiths.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe treatments and management of schizophrenia and delusional disorder (biochemical,
ECT, token economy, CBT).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate treatments and management of schizophrenia and delusional disorder (biochemical,
ECT, token economy, CBT), including a discussion of ethics. 
Psychology and consumer behaviour

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by ‘satisficing’ in consumer decision-making.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe ‘prospect theory’ in consumer decision-making.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain two weaknesses of prospect theory in consumer decision-making.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about selling the product (sales techniques,
interpersonal influence techniques, ways to close a sale).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about selling the product (sales techniques,
interpersonal influence techniques, ways to close a sale), including a discussion on
usefulness. 
Psychology and health

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify two biochemical tests that measure non-adherence in patients.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the procedure used in the study by Chung and Naya (2000) on pill counting.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain two weaknesses of the study by Chung and Naya.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about sources of stress (physiology of stress
and effects on health, and causes of stress).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about sources of stress (physiology of stress
and effects on health, and causes of stress), including a discussion of nature versus nurture.

Psychology and organisations

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by ‘organisational commitment’, e.g. Mowday et al. (1979).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Outline two hygiene factors identified by Herzberg (1959) in the two-factor theory of job
satisfaction.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain one strength and one weakness of the two-factor theory of job satisfaction.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about need theories (hierarchy of needs,
ERG theory, achievement motivation).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about need theories (hierarchy of needs,
ERG theory, achievement motivation), including a discussion of determinism versus free-will.
